traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 203 Myrsinaceae, 204 Theophrastaceae and 295 Primulaceae, which APG joins as Primulaceae: the primroses perennial or annual herbs, the myrsines trees and shrubs (Library 1.0's family is half woody); leaves alternate, opposite or whorled in the primroses, alternate in the myrsines; no stipules; flowers regular, very rarely irregular; corolla united, a tube or a flat wheel, usually 5-lobed (4 or 5 in the woody ones); stamens opposite the petals; ovary superior, rarely half-inferior, of one cell with a free central placenta; fruit a capsule in the primroses, a berry or drupe in the myrsines. The wheel-shaped corolla is read from 'corolla rotate or tubular'.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Primulaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Coridaceae, Theophrastaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded often a basal rosette, often no rosette, sometimes rosettes at the stem tips. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Primulaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Coridaceae, Theophrastaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded usually perennial, sometimes annual, sometimes biennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
